doom.driver: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, officials say, after brief truce. Ukrainian drones attacked a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region early Thursday, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over.
doom.blurb: ENERGY TRUCE SNUFFED OUT AT RYAZAN
doom.summary: The 'energy ceasefire' lasted about as long as a phone battery. Ukrainian drones hit a Ryazan refinery while Kyiv finds its Starshield link throttled and its US intelligence thinned, and nobody can agree on who pulled the plug. Meanwhile the Pentagon is reportedly sizing up the 'mother of all bombs' for Iran, Houthis are pressing Saudi Arabia harder, and a tanker burns off Romania with eight crew missing, so this is less a quiet Thursday than a busy switchboard.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: AI-designed proteins that cut previously unbreakable bonds and a fresh round of on-device agent models show capability marching on, while the money behind it wobbles in a tech sell-off.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Eight states are suing OpenAI over child safety, and the White House reversed a livestreamed military execution only after an outcry, which is not a sign of a steady hand.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: The Russia-Ukraine energy truce has collapsed, US strike options on Iran include its largest non-nuclear bomb, Yemen fighting is intensifying, and suspected sabotage is hitting Starlink sites in NATO countries.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Experts say the recent reports of AI agents hacking stem from frontier labs skipping basic containment rather than models going rogue, which is not as comforting as it sounds.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: AI-assisted Russian and Chinese cyberattacks on UK infrastructure, zero-click spyware delivered through online ads, and a recording device hidden in toilet paper inside OpenAI round out a very spy-heavy day.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Extreme close-up filling the whole frame: the dead glass face of a diesel pump at a roadside fuel station on the flat Oka lowlands outside Ryazan, in the hour before a mid-October dawn. The environment exists only in the reflections and at the edges. A black, curved glass display panel dominates the center, its seven-segment price digits dark and dead, with a few stuck segments flickering faint ember red. Across the glass, a distorted reflection shows the world behind the camera: a thin line of bare birches, a rail spur, a power-line pylon, and a swollen blood-orange glow smeared along the horizon with a column of soot-black smoke bending the sky. Along the bottom edge, the heavy black rubber hose and a frost-rimed steel diesel nozzle hang in a scuffed cradle with chipped yellow-black hazard stripes, lit from below by the volcanic orange light. Wedged into the cradle beside the nozzle is a folded, damp sheet of newsprint carrying only a blurred blocky photo of a flame silhouette and abstract gray bars in place of text, one corner curling in the heat of the reflected glow. A hand-taped cardboard sign dangles from the pump, scrawled with a single crossed-out slash mark and no legible letters. The palette is blood orange and deep black only, with ember highlights on wet metal and cracked glass, crushed pitch-black shadows, and cool tones nearly extinguished. Chunky dithered pixel shading and hard stepped color bands.

dawn.driver: Pig kidneys that were “frozen” for a year have been brought back to life. Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists. They hope to replicate the findin
dawn.blurb: ONE YEAR ON ICE, KIDNEYS WORKING
dawn.summary: Kidneys chilled to -150 °C and kept in a freezer for a year have been rewarmed and shown to work again, the first time anyone has pulled this off. Scientists hope the technique will one day let donated organs be banked rather than raced against the clock, so more patients get the transplant they need. Elsewhere, Brazil's Congress voted for a 40-hour week that could give up to 30 million workers their weekends back, and firefighters in Cobb County, Georgia, helped a vet hospital deliver 15 puppies.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Frozen pig kidneys revived after a year in storage could open the door to organ banking for transplants.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: After talks in Beijing, China signaled that rare earths will keep flowing steadily to the European Union.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Brazil wrote a 40-hour week into its constitution and ended six-day workweeks for up to 30 million people.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Researchers engineered a plant immune receptor that offers a new defense for rice, wheat and barley crops.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Cobb County firefighters answered a call to help a veterinary hospital bring 15 puppies into the world.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. SILHOUETTE COMPOSITION inside a wide, high-ceilinged university transplant surgery suite. A huge wall of frosted-glass light panels blazes behind everything in clear golden-yellow, fading to fresh spring green at the edges, and floods the room with balanced, steady daylight-bright warmth. The foreground is dark, crisp, blue-black silhouettes. In the center, a lone transplant surgeon in scrubs and a cap stands in profile, hands lowered, pausing at the edge of the operating table as if absorbing a big moment. Beside the surgeon, on a steel stand against the glow, a clear perfusion chamber holds a single pig kidney. It is half pale and glass-like, with icy silver-white frost along its edge, and it blushes toward living rose and amber at its core. Tiny golden pixel specks glow inside the tissue like waking embers, showing nanoparticles warming it from within. A curl of frost-white vapor spills from the chamber base. Along the left wall, a row of tall cryogenic freezers stands in silhouette with pale mist drifting from their lids, and a few small organ canisters sit waiting on a shelf. Thin tubes loop from the chamber, and a coiled copper induction ring wraps around it, both traced in sharp rim light. Rim-lit edges, a long soft shadow across the tiled floor, and a feeling of calm, confident dawn rather than a finish line.
